analysis.title: Webinar: Rates outlook 2027 – The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
key_insights: ING promotes a webinar on 4 November 2026 on US and euro rates scenarios for 2027. The note poses scenarios and questions, and publishes no forecasts.
The note asks whether the US 10-year Treasury yield could reach 6% in 2027, and says that outcome is not as far-fetched as it sounds.
The note names three forces that could keep global rates under upward pressure: AI and productivity, extraordinary fiscal deficits, and stubborn inflation.
The note asks what Treasury Secretary Bessent could do if yields surge, and what happens if inflation proves stickier than market expectations suggest.

For the eurozone, the note asks whether the inflation shock is changing rather than disappearing, and whether second-round inflation pressures, heavy bond supply and rising global real rates complicate the outlook even if the ECB turns more dovish.
The note flags France's growing debt challenge as a further source of uncertainty for euro sovereign bond markets, and asks whether bond supply will test investor appetite.

macro_indicators.interpretation: ING raises 6% as a possible scenario for the webinar to discuss. The note does not present it as a forecast.

risk_factors: Global rates could face upward pressure from AI-driven growth, extraordinary fiscal deficits and stubborn inflation.
Second-round inflation pressures, heavy bond supply and rising global real rates could complicate the euro rates outlook even if the ECB turns more dovish.
France's debt challenge could add stress to euro sovereign bond markets, and heavy bond supply could test investor appetite.
geopolitical: France's growing debt challenge is flagged as a source of uncertainty for euro sovereign markets.

key_data_points.context: Posed as a question in the webinar promotion. The note says it is not as far-fetched as it sounds and gives no forecast.
key_data_points.anchor: The US 10-year Treasury hitting 6% in 2027 is not as far-fetched as it sounds.

tension_points.bull_case: Less dramatic outcome: the note raises the possibility that the 6% scenario is overblown and rates land in a less dramatic place.
tension_points.bear_case: AI and productivity, extraordinary fiscal deficits and stubborn inflation combine to keep global rates under upward pressure, potentially pushing the 10-year to 6%.
